text:
maria: quick heads-up — after the 0a1b2c kernel-selector deploy we see a perf regression on short prompts, p99 latency +18% and throughput -7% in the small prompt cohort. suspect admission + kernel flip interaction. anyone on this?

sam: saw the dashboards, digging into profiler now. initial findings: kv-hit-rate for small prompts dropped from 92% -> 76% on canary nodes. batch sizes also shrank median 6 -> 3. decode-rate distribution skewed higher (more token/sec attempts) which messed up the sampler.

kevin: timeline wise that commit changed kernel preference for small sequence-lengths (opt for fused-kv kernel). might have changed scheduling microbeats. cc @aisha for queue policy overlap.

maria: exact numbers from the regression run (20k requests sampled):
```
cohort: short (<64 tokens)
samples: 20,312
p50 latency: 42ms -> 45ms
p95 latency: 120ms -> 137ms
p99 latency: 310ms -> 366ms
median batch size: 6 -> 3
kv cache hit rate: 92.1% -> 76.4%
tokens/sec per request: 420 -> 510 (median)
```

aisha: hmm KV hit drop explains the token throughput bump (more cache misses = more decoding work). the batcher classifier probably reclassified those as higher-decode-rate cohorts, shrinking batch formation window.

sam: profiler trace (example request):
```
[trace] enqueue_wait: 18ms
admission_check: 2.3ms (classifier eval)
batch_wait: 7.1ms
kern_dispatch(fused-kv): 120ms
kernel_total: 130ms
kv_miss_fetch: 95ms
```

maria: interesting that kern_dispatch increased with fused-kv on these misses. maybe fused kernel has worse path for repeated kv-miss cold paths. fallback to non-fused might be cheaper for misses.

kevin: confirmed — benchmark microkernel for fused-kv shows perf wins on warm-cache but ~1.2-1.6x slower on cold kv misses for sequence<64. we can gate fused-kv by predicted kv-hit probability from classifier.

sam: proposal: adjust continuous-batcher heuristics to incorporate a kv-hit probability estimate and decode-rate bucketing. practical changes:
- increase token_budget_target for short prompts from 256 -> 384 to allow slightly larger batches
- add kv-hit-prob threshold: if predicted hit < 0.85, choose fallback kernel and prefer slower admission (longer batch window)
- refine decode-rate buckets: {high:>600 tps, mid:200-600, low:<200} and bias admission to favor grouping mid/low

aisha: sounds reasonable. also recommend adding a short A/B canary: control current policy vs policy-v2 with the 3 changes above. run for 6h across 5% traffic, collect p50/p95/p99, batch size, kv-hit, and cost delta.

perf-bot: automated regression alert attached: job=perf-sweep-172502, compare=baseline->canary, delta.p99=+18%, delta.throughput=-7%, alerted=TRUE

ops-bot: deploy metadata: rollout 0a1b2c at 2024-05-12T14:02Z, canary nodes pool=canary-3, region=us-west2

kevin: I'll open a quick PR that gates fused-kv by predicted hit. will add feature flag `kernel.kv_gate_v1` and feature-config to console.

maria: assigning action items:
- kevin: kernel gate PR + perf microbench (ETA today EOD)
- aisha: run A/B canary with new batcher heuristics, record metrics (ETA tomorrow morning)
- sam: add kv-hit prob model export to classifier service and instrument sampling (ETA today)

sam: small request — when running canary, enable detailed traces for 1% of matched requests to capture kv-miss stack and kernel timings.

aisha: yep will enable trace-sampling=1% for the experiment. also will add a cheap synthetic workload that exercises short prompts + kv miss to stress path.

maria: if the experiments validate we can roll kernel gate + batcher policy together. goal: recover p99 within 5% of baseline and not increase cost by >3%.

kevin: quick note — I found related commit in 0a1b2c that also tweaked admission timeout from 6ms->4ms for small queues. might need to revert that if increasing token_budget. adding that to PR comment.

sam: thanks — tracking test matrix in the ticket: INF-2047. will post results in this thread when done. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all — great triage. keeping thread open for results.
